response.sql: WITH grouped AS (SELECT ili.order_item_id AS order_item_id, p.product_color AS product_color, AVG(CAST(ili.product_quantity AS REAL)) AS avg_quantity, AVG((ili.derived_product_cost - ili.derived_total_cost) / NULLIF(ili.derived_total_cost, 0)) AS avg_cost_ratio FROM Invoice_Line_Items ili JOIN Order_Items oi ON oi.order_item_id = ili.order_item_id JOIN Products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY ili.order_item_id, p.product_color), ranked AS (SELECT order_item_id, product_color, avg_quantity, avg_cost_ratio, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY product_color ORDER BY avg_quantity DESC NULLS LAST) AS quantity_rank FROM grouped) SELECT order_item_id, product_color, avg_quantity, avg_cost_ratio, quantity_rank FROM ranked WHERE quantity_rank <= 3;

assumptions.assumption: The database is SQLite (the schema uses SQLite-style types). The query needs SQLite 3.30+ for NULLS LAST and window functions.
product_quantity is stored as numeric text, so it is cast to REAL before averaging. Non-numeric strings would break the average.
A derived_total_cost of 0 makes the cost ratio undefined, so it is treated as a missing value (NULLIF) and ignored in the average rather than raising a division error.
Products with a NULL product_color form their own color group and are ranked within that group.
Each order item maps to one product, so each (order_item_id, color) group is one order item. Ranks use RANK(), so ties share a rank and the next rank is skipped. NULL averages sort last.
